items.title: SIU Probes Mississauga Incident Involving Police and Pedestrian
items.summary: A concerning incident in Mississauga has prompted an investigation by Ontario’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU). On Sunday, a person was struck by a vehicle on Viscount Road, between Network Road and Highway 409, during a police presence. According to Const. Tyler Bell from Peel Regional Police, officers were initially responding to a report of a disturbance involving two individuals fighting in the roadway. While police were on the scene, one of the individuals was hit by a passing vehicle. Fortunately, the injuries sustained were not serious. The police have closed the road in the area while investigations continue, ensuring there is no threat to the community. The SIU, which investigates incidents involving police where there is death, serious injury, or allegations of sexual assault, is now looking into the circumstances surrounding this event. This highlights the critical nature of motor vehicle accident investigations and the importance of understanding pedestrian and police interactions in such contexts. The SIU is investigating due to police presence during the incident. The accident occurred on Viscount Road, Mississauga. Police were responding to a disturbance call at the time. For residents in Ontario, this incident underscores the importance of understanding your rights when involved in or witnessing a motor vehicle accident. When police are present, it is crucial to be aware of how their actions can impact the outcomes of such incidents.

items.title: SIU investigating after 1 person hit by driver in Mississauga while police were present
items.summary: Ontario’s police watchdog has invoked its mandate after one person was hit by the driver of a vehicle in the presence of the police on Sunday in Mississauga. Const. Tyler Bell, of Peel Regional Police, said he is limited in what details he can share about what occurred. “Officers responded to the area following reports of a disturbance involving two individuals fighting in the roadway,” he wrote in an email to CP24. “During the incident, one of the individuals was struck by a passing vehicle. , police issued a traffic alert on X, advising motorists of a road closure on Viscount Road between Network Road and Highway 409. Drivers are being advised to use alternate routes. The road has since reopened. They said this is an ongoing police investigation and there is no threat to the community. items.title: 2 men stabbed during ‘parking dispute’ in Mississauga, police say
items.summary: Two men were seriously injured in a stabbing in Mississauga Saturday evening, police say. m. following reports of an altercation and possible stabbing. Officers arrived and found two men suffering from stab wounds. Both were taken to hospital with serious injuries and are now in stable condition. Police say the incident followed a reported parking dispute. Officers searched the area and located one of the suspects shortly afterward. Ali Halimi, 30, of Mississauga, was arrested and charged with assault. A second man, who police believe stabbed the victims and may be in possession of the knife, remains outstanding and is wanted for attempted murder. He is described as Middle Eastern, approximately 25 to 35 years old, with a thin build, medium complexion, thinning brown hair and an unshaven appearance.

items.title: 361 assaults reported to police in the last 31 days in Mississauga and Brampton
items.summary: There were over 350 assault-related crimes reported to police in Mississauga and Brampton last month. From July 30 to Aug 30, Peel Regional Police data indicates that 361 assaults were reported, including 140 in Mississauga, 214 in Brampton, one in Burlington, one in Caledon and two incidents in Toronto that fell under Peel jurisdiction. This works out to an average of 11 or more of these crimes being committed daily. items.title: Stabbing: 2 men sent to hospital in Mississauga, one man arrested
items.summary: Two men were seriously injured in a stabbing in Mississauga Saturday evening, police say. m. following reports of an altercation and possible stabbing. Police later confirmed in a social media post that two men had been stabbed. Both were taken to hospital with serious injuries. Updates on their conditions are unknown. Additional information about the victims, including their ages, places of residence, and whether they were known to the suspects, has not been released. Investigators say a man was taken into custody, while police continued to search the area for a possible second suspect. Police have not shared details about the altercation that led to the stabbing. The public was asked to avoid the area as the investigation continued.

items.title: Mississauga Pesäpallo Players Set Sights on World Cup in Sydney This October
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, a Mississauga-based community group is hoping to eventually bring the Pesäpallo World Cup to the city after building a growing following for Finland's national sport locally. The outlet reports a group of Greater Toronto Area residents, some travelling from as far as Oakville and Burlington, regularly gather at Bloor Athletic Field in Mississauga to play the sport. Mississauga.com describes pesäpallo as a fast-paced game resembling baseball, featuring a distinctive field, unusual running patterns and near-constant action that appeals to players of different ages, backgrounds and skill levels. According to the outlet, while some participants treat it purely as a recreational activity, others are preparing to represent Team Canada at the 12th Pesäpallo World Cup in Sydney, Australia, running October 2 to 5 this year. Mississauga.com reports the four-day tournament is being organized by the Finnish Society of Sydney and is expected to draw teams from Australia, Finland, Canada, Germany and India competing in men's, women's and mixed categories.

items.title: Second Suspect in Cooksville Stabbing Sought for Attempted Murder, Police Warn Public Not to Approach
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, one man is in custody and a second remains at large following what police describe as a violent parking dispute that turned into a stabbing in Mississauga over the weekend. The outlet reports two men were found suffering from stab wounds and were taken to hospital with serious injuries, though their condition has since stabilized. According to CityNews Toronto, officers searched the area and arrested 30-year-old Ali Halimi of Mississauga without incident, charging him with assault. The outlet reports detectives are now searching for a second male suspect, believed to have stabbed the victims and to still be in possession of the knife, who is wanted for attempted murder. CityNews Toronto describes the outstanding suspect as Middle Eastern, approximately 25 to 35 years old, with a thin build, medium complexion, thinning brown hair and an unshaven appearance. According to the outlet, police say the suspect should be considered armed and dangerous.

items.title: Cooksville Plaza Stabbing Leaves Two in Hospital, One Suspect in Custody
items.summary: According to CTV News, two people were taken to hospital following an altercation with what police called a possible stabbing at a shopping plaza in Mississauga's Cooksville neighbourhood late Saturday afternoon. The outlet reports the incident happened near Dundas Street West and Parkerhill Road, just west of Hurontario Street. CTV News reports police said the two people suffered serious but non-life-threatening injuries and were taken to separate hospitals, with one sent to a trauma centre. According to the outlet, paramedics described the injuries differently, saying one patient had life-threatening injuries and the other had serious, life-threatening injuries. CTV News reports investigators took one suspect into custody while continuing to work out whether any other suspects remain outstanding. The outlet reports a large police presence remained in the area, with officers advising people to avoid the vicinity.

items.title: SaiGon Pho and Grill Opens Second GTA Location Inside Square One's Food District
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto-based Vietnamese restaurant SaiGon Pho and Grill has opened a second location inside The Food District at Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga. The outlet reports the restaurant serves traditional Vietnamese dishes including slow-simmered pho, grilled pork rice, vermicelli bowls, banh mi sandwiches, spring rolls and grilled meats. INsauga reports the chain's first location opened near Finch Station in Toronto in 2025. According to the outlet, the new Square One location features a dine-in space finished with wood accents and soft lighting. INsauga reports the opening is part of a wave of new restaurants that arrived in Mississauga and the wider region in August, as diners look for new options heading into the fall.
